findings.title: Commit points are written as checkbox tasks, not `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description: Tasks 2C, 3C, 4C, 5C and 6C (lines 71, 94, 117, 126, 134) are `- [ ] **Task NC: Commit**` checklist items. Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**: <message>` lines, never checkboxes. Convert each to a plain marker line after its test task; the placement is already correct.

findings.title: Lint runs only after the three feature commits, and late code fixes land under `docs:` commits
findings.description:
`pnpm lint` first runs in Task 6, after the `feat` commits at 2C, 3C and 4C, so those commits are not at fully checked points. Two later steps can also change code with only a docs commit available:
- **Task 5:** tells the implementer to fix parity bugs and add tests, but its only commit is `docs: record slice 214 parity sweep results`.
- **Task 6:** any lint fix would land under `docs: add cf validate design to command reference`.

Fix: add `pnpm lint` to the Success line of Tasks 2T, 3T and 4T. Give Tasks 5 and 6 a commit message that fits code changes (for example `fix(cli): …` when source changed), with the docs message used only for docs-only changes.

findings.title: Task 4T does not say how to pick designs "that pass the bash script today"
findings.description: The step requires several real slice designs that pass the bash script, but the script is first run in Task 5. A junior implementer is likely to pick files that pass the new command, which makes the test circular and loses the parity intent of the criterion. Add a sub-step to Task 4T: run `./project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/validate-slice-design` over `project-documents/user/slices/*-slice.*.md` and take the test inputs from the files it reports as `PASS`.

findings.title: Some exit-2 conditions are tested only at core level, and "unreadable" is untested
findings.description: Directory-as-file and template-without-markers are asserted in Task 3T but not in Task 4T's exit-2 list (line 113). Unreadable file, unreadable template and the "wrap unexpected `fs` error" path have no test at either level. This is acceptable because the CLI sends one error type through `handleError(err, 2)` and permission-based tests are unreliable in CI. Adding directory-as-file to the 4T list would be a cheap extra check; no new task is needed.

findings.title: Task 0 hard-codes `main` instead of using the configured target
findings.description: Task 0 expects an empty integration branch and stops for the Project Manager otherwise. The branch rules say to fork from the configured target whatever it is. Reword to `git checkout -b 214-slice.native-slice-design-validation {target}` and drop the stop condition.
